law: Hospitals rarely replace their core system of record
evidence: Phase5 bot_incumbent_lockin GREEN 16 cos/209 hits both axes; Phase2 F-2.4 0/19 occupy SoR; Phase8 B2
implication: Build beside the HMIS, never against it (DL-020)

law: Software that cannot complete an action cannot learn from it
evidence: Phase8 R1 self-sealing loop; Phase3 52.4% before-commit vs 12.9% at; Phase8 F-8.2 149 fabricated adapters, zero flywheel
implication: Execution is the precondition for improvement, not its reward

law: Attention follows data availability, not labour intensity
evidence: Phase2 F-2.13 radiology 234 vs nursing 10; Phase4 0/449 platforms mention nursing; Phase6 F-6.3
implication: The biggest gaps are where no digital artifact exists (DL-040)

law: Liability, not capability, bounds automation in healthcare
evidence: Phase6 F-6.4 all 4 highest-stakes units score bottom on liability alone; Phase7 F-7.5; Phase8 B1
implication: Liability allocation is a design variable (DL-041)

law: Standards govern exchange between institutions, never operations inside them
evidence: Phase7 F-7.3: 409/449 FHIR-certified yet 0 coverage of OT/bed/roster/charge-capture; ABDM M1-M3 scope

law: Consumer subscription is the fallback of companies blocked from institutional revenue
evidence: Phase2 F-2.7 19/21 discuss reimbursement but bill consumers; Phase5 churn+CAC both GREEN 11 cos; Phase8 R4
implication: Enter on operational budget, not consumer wallet

law: Trust is manufactured by traceability, not by accuracy claims
evidence: Phase2 F-2.11 provenance 55/citation 55/editorial 50 dominate; Phase5 ai_citation_grounding GREEN 17 cos; Phase7 F-7.4

law: Every layer above the clinician can approve a purchase; only the clinician creates value
evidence: Phase2 F-2.10 CIO 13/CFO 9/committee 8 vs CMIO 1; G01 panel on CMIO requirements

law: Workflow continuity is inversely proportional to institutional depth
evidence: Phase4 F-4.7 patient journey break rate 0.00 at 12.2 owners vs ICU/ED/admin/mgmt 1.00
implication: Opportunity is measured by break rate, not participant count (DL-029)

law: The most crowded capability is usually the least defensible
evidence: Phase7 F-7.1 analytics_dashboard 16 cos = legacy artifact; gamification 12; onboarding 7; conversion 11
implication: Crowding signals a compensating mechanism for a pre-AI limitation

law: Fragmentation of supply raises the value of the interface layer
evidence: Phase2 253 HMIS vendors India vs ~5 US; Phase2 F-2.9 UI automation claimed by 2/21; Phase8 R3

law: Government rails create counterparty networks before products exist
evidence: Phase6 live probe NHCX 38 partners incl 12 insurers + 4 TPAs; ABDM 445 partners, free API
implication: In India the network precedes the product; in the US it must be bought
